properties.name: Leucistic Cambodian
properties.summary: The Cambodian line was first collected by mycologist John W. Allen in cattle pasture around the Angkor Wat temples in the 1990s. The leucistic form is a pale, low-pigment mutation of that same line.

properties.name: Golden Teacher
properties.summary: Golden Teacher surfaced in the late 1980s. Most accounts place the first find in Florida, a few say Georgia, and the exact spot was never recorded. The name comes from its golden-yellow caps.

properties.name: Amazonian
properties.summary: Collected from the Amazon rainforest in Brazil and later isolated as the PES Amazonian line by Pacifica Spora. Known for tall, thick stems and broad caps.

properties.name: Natal Super Strength
properties.summary: Grown around the world for years as Psilocybe natalensis, the NSS line turned out in 2026 to be a species of its own, found on cattle dung in the grasslands of South Africa and Zimbabwe. It is the closest wild relative of cubensis, and the two split about 1.5 million years ago.
